items.detail: With US cash markets shut for the weekend after Friday's jobs-driven, record-setting week, attention pivots to the calendar: **S&P 500 futures sit near 7,775** and **July CPI on Wednesday, Aug 12** now shapes up as the pivotal test of the market's freshly revived Fed-easing bet.
Economists see **July headline CPI accelerating to ~3.6% year-on-year** (from 3.2%) on a hot **+0.6% monthly** print, even as **core CPI eases to roughly 4.3%** — its lowest in about two years.
items.why: A projected ~5.9% surge in energy costs, tied to oil's climb back toward the low-$80s, is expected to drive the headline pickup while shelter and core disinflation continue.

items.detail: Rate expectations hardened further over the weekend: **Polymarket now prices a September Fed hold at about 66%** (up from ~50% before the jobs data), while the odds of any 2026 rate hike slid to **56% from a recent 77%**.
items.why: Friday's surprise 23,000-payroll drop continues to reprice the policy path toward steady-to-easier, extending the shift that lifted stocks into the weekend.

items.detail: Gold extended its record run, **up about 7.5% this week** — outpacing Bitcoin (+4.6%) and the S&P 500 (+2.9%) since Monday.
items.why: Weaker jobs data and rising Fed rate-cut expectations, alongside a softer dollar, fueled a broad haven and liquidity bid that favored non-yielding assets, with gold the standout.

items.detail: A light earnings week (Super Micro, Applied Materials, Tapestry, Cardinal Health) sets up around the marquee macro double-header: **July CPI on Wednesday and July retail sales on Friday, Aug 14**.

Indian equities enter the new week riding a **second straight weekly gain**, with the Nifty 50 holding above its **50-, 100- and 200-week EMAs** and a **weekly RSI of 52.45** signaling that bullish momentum stays intact despite ongoing consolidation.

Foreign inflows remain the structural prop beneath the recovery: FII buying that has reached **~$1.3 billion in August** (after $2.1 billion in July) has been aided by crude's retreat from the $90-plus danger zone toward **$83-85**.
items.why: Sustained overseas appetite plus cooler oil have kept the medium-term uptrend intact even after Friday's private-bank-led dip, an ongoing continuation of last week's support.

items.detail: Next week's direction hinges on global cues — chiefly **US July CPI (Aug 12)** and crude prices — after an IT-sector resurgence and firm autos cushioned the financials-led weakness that closed out the prior week.

Bitcoin is consolidating just below resistance into the weekend, trading around **$64,718** (a $64,124-$65,312 range) after Friday's jobs-driven pop above $65K, while **Ether holds roughly $1,900-1,930**.
items.why: With US markets shut, momentum has stalled at the well-defended $65,000 zone that has repeatedly capped BTC, leaving traders cautious ahead of a data-heavy week.

items.detail: **Solana outperformed, spiking as high as $83.50** and holding above $80 after recovering from lows near $60 — its strongest levels since entering July around $67.
items.why: Relentless US spot Solana-ETF demand, with positive net inflows on every July trading day and over $1 billion in cumulative flows since launch, has driven the outperformance.

items.detail: Crypto's tape is now firmly macro-led: with **September Fed-hold odds jumping to ~66%**, Bitcoin is **+4.6% since Monday**, moving in lockstep with gold (+7.5%) and stocks (+2.9%).
items.why: Friday's weak payrolls reset rate expectations, leaving Fed policy and Wednesday's CPI — not crypto-specific news — as the swing factor for BTC and ETH.

items.detail: On the product and policy front, **21Shares' TSOL Solana fund will switch its pricing benchmark to the FTSE Digital Assets Index effective Aug 24**, while the stalled CLARITY Act keeps a federal crypto framework off the table until the Senate returns from recess on Sept 11.

crossCuttingTheme: Friday's shock jobs miss remains the master switch, and its weekend echo is a broad liquidity-driven melt-up in non-yielding and risk assets alike — gold (+7.5% on the week) leading Bitcoin (+4.6%) and the S&P 500 (+2.9%) since Monday as September Fed-hold odds jump to ~66% — with all eyes now on Wednesday's July CPI, where an energy-driven headline jump toward 3.6% could test the market's freshly minted bet on a Fed that holds rather than hikes.
